items.title: How much genuinely useful signal do more raw-monitoring hours actually buy?
items.description: Elena spends about 10 hours a week reading raw feeds directly. Assume a fast-moving field only produces a small, roughly fixed amount of genuinely useful signal each week (regardless of how much raw material surrounds it), and that more monitoring time finds a larger share of it — but with fast early gains that taper off hard. Drag the slider to see how little extra signal Elena's later hours actually buy compared to her first few.
items.compute: const ceiling = 2; const rate = 0.3; const usefulSignals = params.hoursPerWeek === 0 ? 0 : ceiling * (1 - Math.exp(-rate * params.hoursPerWeek)); return { usefulSignals: Math.round(usefulSignals * 100) / 100 };

outputs.label: Genuinely useful items surfaced per week
